item.title: How to get your international driver's license in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
If you're planning to drive abroad, you may need an International Driving Permit (IDP) in addition to your South African driver's license. An IDP is a legally recognized document that translates your driver's license information into multiple languages, making it easier for foreign authorities to verify your driving credentials. In this guide, we'll explain who needs an IDP, how to apply for one, and how to get your required photos quickly and easily.

Who needs an IDP?

South African citizens who intend to drive in foreign countries should obtain an International Driving Permit. While an IDP is not a substitute for your domestic driver's license, it serves as an official translation recognized in over 150 countries worldwide. You'll need to carry both your South African driver's license and your IDP when driving abroad. It's important to note that IDP requirements vary by country, so check the specific regulations of your destination before traveling.

How to apply for an IDP

To apply for an International Driving Permit in South Africa, follow these steps:

  1. Ensure you have a valid South African driver's license. Your license must be current and unexpired throughout the duration of your international travel.
  2. Gather the required documents. These are outlined in the next paragraph.
  3. Submit your application in person at an Automobile Association of South Africa (AA) branch or by mail to the AA head office in Johannesburg. The AA is the authorized issuer of IDPs in South Africa.
  4. Pay the applicable fees for your IDP.
  5. Wait for your IDP to be processed and issued. You can collect it in person or have it mailed to you, depending on your preference.

Documents required

When applying for your South African IDP, you'll need to submit the following documents:

  • Your original valid South African driver's license
  • A certified copy of your driver's license
  • Two identical passport-sized photographs
  • A completed IDP application form (available from AA branches or online)
  • Proof of payment for the IDP fee

Passport photo requirements

The passport-sized photographs for your IDP application must adhere to the following specifications:

  • Photos must be 35mm wide x 45mm high
  • Taken against a plain white or light gray background
  • Printed on high-quality photographic paper
  • Clear, in focus, and showing your full face looking directly at the camera
  • Taken within the past 6 months to reflect your current appearance
  • No hats, sunglasses, or other accessories obscuring your face
  • Digital photos are accepted if they meet the quality and size requirements

Processing time and validity

Once the Automobile Association receives your complete IDP application, processing typically takes 2-3 working days. However, this timeline may vary depending on the volume of applications being processed at the time. It's best to apply for your IDP well in advance of your planned travel dates to allow sufficient time for processing and delivery. Your South African International Driving Permit is valid for one year from the date of issue, after which you'll need to renew it if you plan to continue driving abroad.

Cost of an IDP in South Africa

As of 2024, the cost of obtaining an International Driving Permit in South Africa is R349. This fee is payable to the Automobile Association when submitting your application. The price includes the processing and issuing of your IDP, as well as any applicable taxes. Keep in mind that additional costs may be incurred for certifying copies of your driver's license and obtaining passport-sized photographs.

Get your IDP photos quickly with Smartphone iD

When applying for your South African International Driving Permit, you'll need two identical passport-sized photographs. Smartphone iD makes it simple and affordable to get high-quality, compliant photos right from your smartphone. Just download the Smartphone iD app and take your photo following our clear guidelines.

Subsequently, our team of biometric experts and advanced AI system will ensure your photo meets the official requirements. You'll then receive a digital copy to print or a set of physical prints delivered directly to your doorstep. This entire process will only take a couple of minutes of your time!

Where to collect your IDP

You have two options for receiving your International Driving Permit once it has been processed by the Automobile Association:

  1. In-person collection: You can collect your IDP at any AA branch nationwide. Be sure to bring your original driver's license and proof of identity for verification purposes.
  2. Mail delivery: If you prefer, you can request to have your IDP mailed to your provided address. The AA will send your permit via registered mail, and you'll need to sign for the package upon receipt.

The choice between in-person collection and mail delivery depends on your personal preference. If you need your IDP urgently, in-person collection may be the faster option. However, if you live far from an AA branch, mail delivery can save you the trip.

item.title: How to get your disabled parking disc in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
If you have a disability that affects your mobility, you may be eligible for a disabled parking disc in South Africa. This permit allows you to park in designated disabled parking spaces, making it easier to access businesses, public facilities, and other destinations. In this guide, we'll cover the eligibility requirements, application process, and how Smartphone iD can assist you in obtaining your parking disc quickly and conveniently.

Disabled parking disc eligibility

To qualify for a disabled parking disc in South Africa, you must have a permanent or temporary mobility impairment that significantly restricts your ability to walk. This includes conditions such as:

  • Paraplegia or quadriplegia
  • Amputation of a lower limb
  • Severe arthritis or joint damage in the lower limbs
  • Neurological conditions affecting mobility (e.g., multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease)
  • Cardiovascular or respiratory disorders that severely limit walking ability

Your medical condition must be certified by a registered medical practitioner, who should complete the necessary forms as part of your application.

How to apply

To apply for a disabled parking disc in South Africa, follow the following steps:

  1. Obtain the application form (MR1) from your local Driving License Testing Centre (DLTC) or download it from the relevant provincial government website.
  2. Have your medical practitioner complete the medical certificate portion of the form, confirming your disability and its impact on your mobility.
  3. Fill out the rest of the application form with your personal details and contact information.
  4. Gather the required supporting documents (see below).
  5. Submit your completed application, medical certificate, supporting documents, and applicable fees to your nearest DLTC.
  6. Wait for your application to be processed. If approved, you'll be notified to collect your disabled parking disc from the DLTC.

Required documents

When applying for a disabled parking disc, you'll need to submit the following:

  • Completed application form (MR1) with medical certificate
  • Your original valid South African ID book or card
  • Certified copy of your ID book or card
  • Two identical passport-sized photographs 
  • Proof of residential address (e.g., utility bill, bank statement)
  • Applicable fees (vary by province)

Passport photo requirements

The passport-sized photographs for your disabled parking disc application must meet these specifications:

  • Photos must be 35mm wide x 45mm high
  • Taken against a plain white or light gray background
  • Printed on high-quality photographic paper
  • Clear, in focus, and showing your full face looking directly at the camera
  • Taken within the past 6 months to reflect your current appearance
  • No hats, sunglasses, or other accessories obscuring your face
  • Digital photos are accepted if they meet the quality and size requirements

Cost and validity

The cost of obtaining a disabled parking disc in South Africa varies by province, but generally ranges from R50 to R100. This fee is payable when submitting your application at the DLTC. Your disabled parking disc is typically valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue, after which you'll need to renew it. If your disability is temporary, your disc may be issued for a shorter period aligned with your expected recovery time.

Processing time and collection

The processing time for disabled parking disc applications can vary depending on the province and the volume of applications being handled. Generally, expect to wait 2-4 weeks for your application to be reviewed and approved. Once your disc is ready, you'll be contacted to collect it from the DLTC where you submitted your application. Be sure to bring your original ID book or card for verification when collecting your disc.

Get your disabled parking disc photos quickly with Smartphone iD

With the Smartphone iD app, you can take your passport photos from the comfort of your own home within just a few minutes. Our advanced AI and our team of biometric experts will review your photos to ensure they meet the required specifications. If any issues arise, we'll guide you through the process until you have the perfect shot.

At a fraction of the cost of traditional photo studios, Smartphone iD offers a convenient and reliable solution to take your passport photo all by yourself. Download the app now and secure your disabled parking disc without a hassle!

In this article, we'll guide you through the process of completing your online passport application and explain how we can help you get the perfect passport photo to include with your application.

How to get an online passport application in South Africa

The eHomeAffairs online portal is currently only available for South African citizens by birth. To access the online passport application system, follow these steps:

  1. Create an account on the eHomeAffairs website.
  2. Log in to your account and navigate to the passport application section.
  3. Fill out the required personal information and upload scanned copies of your supporting documents as instructed by the system.
  4. Pay the passport application fee online using a credit or debit card.

After completing the online portion of the application, you may still need to visit a Department of Home Affairs office in person to finalize the process. This typically involves submitting original documents and potentially having your fingerprints or photo taken if they were not captured digitally during the online application.

How to apply for your passport online

To apply for your South African passport online, follow these steps:

  1. Gather all the necessary documents, including your South African ID book or smart ID card, your birth certificate, and proof of address.
  2. Log in to your eHomeAffairs account and navigate to the passport application section.
  3. Fill out the required personal information and upload scanned copies of your supporting documents as instructed by the system.

item.title: How to get a new passport in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Are you a South African citizen in need of a new passport? Whether your current passport has expired or you're applying for the first time, the process of obtaining a new passport can seem daunting. In this article, we'll guide you through the steps of applying for a new passport in South Africa, including the required documents, costs, and processing times. 

When to apply for a new passport in South Africa

It's important to note that South African passports cannot be renewed. They are valid for a set period - 10 years for adults and 5 years for children. Once your passport expires, you need to submit a completely new application for a fresh passport through the Department of Home Affairs. It's recommended to start the application process several months before your current passport expires to avoid any travel disruptions.

How to apply for a new South African passport

To apply for a new South African passport, follow these five simple steps:

  1. Gather all the necessary documents required for your passport application (see paragraph below).
  2. Visit your nearest Department of Home Affairs office in person, as online or mail applications are not accepted.
  3. Fill out the passport application form accurately and completely, double-checking all information to avoid delays.
  4. Submit your supporting documents and provide your biometric data (fingerprints and photograph) at the office.
  5. Pay the passport application fee and wait for processing, which typically takes 7-10 working days, before collecting your new passport.

Required documents for a new passport application

When applying for a new South African passport, you'll need to provide the following documents:

  1. A completed passport application form (DHA-73)
  2. Your original birth certificate or ID document
  3. Proof of citizenship, such as a naturalization certificate (if applicable)
  4. Two identical passport photographs that meet the Department of Home Affairs' requirements
  5. Proof of payment for the passport fee

Make sure to double-check the requirements and have all your documents in order before visiting the Department of Home Affairs office.

Passport application costs and processing times

The current cost for a new South African passport is R400 for adults and R200 for children under 16 years old. The Department of Home Affairs aims to process passport applications within 7-10 working days, but it's advisable to allow for extra time in case of any unforeseen delays. If you need your passport urgently, you can opt for the expedited service, which comes at an additional cost.

Get your passport photo quickly with Smartphone iD

This is where our app, Smartphone iD, comes in handy. With Smartphone iD, you can take your passport photo from the comfort of your own home using your smartphone camera. 

Our app guides you through the process, ensuring that your photo meets all the necessary requirements. Plus, our team of biometric experts and advanced AI system check each photo to guarantee compliance. Download the app now and receive your passport photos within minutes!

item.title: How to get a Schengen Visa in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Are you a South African citizen planning to travel to Europe? If so, you'll need to obtain a Schengen visa before your trip. The Schengen visa allows you to enter and travel freely within the 26 countries that make up the Schengen Area. In this guide, we'll walk you through the process of applying for a Schengen visa in South Africa, including the requirements, application steps, and helpful tips to ensure a smooth application process.

Who can apply for a Schengen visa?

South African citizens who wish to travel to any of the 26 Schengen countries for tourism, business, or other short-term purposes need to apply for a Schengen visa. The Schengen Area includes countries such as France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and many others. It's important to note that a Schengen visa is not required for South Africans traveling to non-Schengen countries like the United Kingdom or Ireland.

Where to apply for a Schengen visa in South Africa

To apply for a Schengen visa, you'll need to submit your application at the embassy or consulate of the Schengen country you plan to visit. If you're visiting multiple Schengen countries, you should apply at the embassy or consulate of the country where you'll be spending the most time. In some cases, you may need to apply through a visa application center authorized by the embassy or consulate.

How to apply for a Schengen visa

To apply for a Schengen visa, follow these five steps:

  1. Determine the type of Schengen visa you need based on the purpose and duration of your trip, such as a tourist visa, business visa, or student visa.
  2. Gather all the necessary documents, including a valid passport, completed visa application form, passport-size photos, travel itinerary, proof of accommodation, proof of financial means, and any other required documents specific to your visa type.
  3. Schedule an appointment at the embassy or consulate of the Schengen country you plan to visit, or the country where you will spend the most time during your trip.
  4. Attend your visa appointment, submit your application and supporting documents, pay the visa fee, and participate in an interview if required.
  5. Wait for the processing of your Schengen visa application, which can take up to 15 days, and collect your passport with the visa once it's approved.

Passport photo requirements for a Schengen visa

When applying for a Schengen visa, you'll need to submit two recent passport-size photos. The photos must meet specific requirements, such as being taken against a light background, having a neutral facial expression, and meeting the correct dimensions. Using our Smartphone iD app, you can easily take and print your passport photos from the comfort of your home, ensuring they meet all the necessary requirements.

Documents required for a Schengen visa application

When applying for a Schengen visa, you'll need to submit the following documents: 

  • Valid passport
  • Two recent passport-size photos
  • Completed visa application form
  • Proof of travel insurance
  • Flight reservations
  • Hotel bookings or proof of accommodation
  • Cover letter explaining the purpose of your trip
  • Proof of employment
  • Financial documents demonstrating sufficient funds for your stay

The exact documents needed may vary depending on the embassy or consulate where you apply and your individual circumstances. Always check with the specific embassy or consulate for the most up-to-date information on required documents for your Schengen visa application.

Processing time for a Schengen visa

The processing time for a Schengen visa can vary depending on the embassy or consulate where you apply, as well as the time of year and the volume of applications they receive. On average, you can expect to receive a decision on your visa application within 15 days. However, it's always a good idea to apply well in advance of your planned travel date to allow for any unexpected delays.

Schengen visa cost for South Africans

As of 2024, the standard Schengen visa fee for South African citizens is €80. This fee is non-refundable, even if your application is rejected. Some applicants, such as children under 12 years old or students participating in educational trips, may be eligible for a reduced fee or fee waiver. Be sure to check with the embassy or consulate for the most up-to-date information on visa fees and any applicable reductions.

Get your Schengen visa photo quickly with Smartphone iD

At Smartphone iD, we understand that applying for a Schengen visa can be a daunting process. That's why we've developed our app to make taking and printing your passport photos as easy and stress-free as possible. With our app, you can take your photos using your smartphone camera, and our advanced AI system will check them to ensure they meet all the necessary biometric requirements. 

Faqs

1. Do I need a Schengen visa to visit Europe from South Africa?

Yes, South African citizens need to obtain a Schengen visa to enter and travel within the 26 countries that make up the Schengen Area.

2. What types of Schengen visas are available for South Africans?

South Africans can apply for various types of Schengen visas, including tourist visas, business visas, student visas, and visas for medical treatment.

3. Which embassy/consulate should I apply to?

You should apply at the embassy or consulate of the Schengen country where you plan to spend the most time during your trip.

4. How do I schedule a visa appointment?

To schedule a visa appointment, contact the embassy or consulate directly or visit their website for information on their appointment booking system.

5. Is there a visa interview? What should I expect?

Some Schengen visa applications may require an in-person interview. During the interview, you'll be asked about your travel plans, financial situation, and ties to your home country.

6. Can my Schengen visa application be rejected?

Yes, a Schengen visa application can be rejected for various reasons, such as insufficient documentation, unclear travel purpose, or concerns about your intention to return to South Africa.

7. Which passport photo app for Schengen visa?

Our Smartphone iD app is the perfect solution for taking and printing your Schengen visa passport photos. It's easy to use, affordable, and ensures your photos meet all the necessary requirements.

8. What type of passport photo is required for a Schengen visa?

Schengen visa passport photos must be recent, taken against a light background, have a neutral facial expression, and meet specific size requirements. With Smartphone iD, you can be confident that your photos will be accepted by the embassy or consulate.

item.title: How to Renew Your South African ID Card
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Are you wondering how to renew your South African ID card? The current green bar-coded ID cards are valid for 10 years, and once they expire, you need to apply for a new one rather than renewing the old card. The process may seem daunting, but don't worry - we've got you covered with all the details you need to know to apply for your new ID card smoothly.

When to apply for a new ID card

Your current South African ID card is valid for 10 years from the date of issue. It's important to keep track of when your ID card expires so you can apply for a new one before it becomes invalid. We recommend starting the application process at least a month before your current ID card expires to ensure you receive your new one in time.

Where to apply for a new ID card

You can apply for a new South African ID card at any Department of Home Affairs office across the country. Be sure to check the operating hours of your local office and arrive early to avoid long wait times. Some offices may also allow you to schedule an appointment in advance, which can save you time on the day of your application.

How to apply for a new ID Card

Follow the following steps to renew your South African ID card:

  1. Obtain and complete the DHA-9 application form from a Department of Home Affairs office or their website.
  2. Gather required supporting documents, including your original birth certificate, proof of residential address, and current ID card (if applicable).
  3. Submit your completed application form and supporting documents at your local Department of Home Affairs office, and pay the application fee (currently R140).
  4. Provide your biometric information, such as fingerprints and photograph, which will be captured by the Department of Home Affairs official.
  5. Wait for your new ID card to be processed and delivered to your specified collection point, which typically takes 4-6 weeks from the date of application.

Required documents for an ID card application

When applying for a new South African ID card, you'll need to provide certain documents to prove your identity and eligibility. These include:

  • Your original birth certificate
  • Proof of your residential address (e.g., a utility bill or bank statement)
  • Your current ID card (if you have one)
  • A completed DHA-9 application form

Cost of a new ID card

As of 2024, the cost of a new South African ID card is R140. This fee must be paid at the time of application and can be paid via cash, credit card, or debit card at most Department of Home Affairs offices. Keep in mind that fees are subject to change, so it's always a good idea to check the current cost before applying.

Processing time for a new ID card

The processing time for a new South African ID card can vary depending on the volume of applications being processed at the time. Typically, you can expect to receive your new ID card within 4-6 weeks of submitting your application. If you haven't received your card within this timeframe, you can check the status of your application online or by contacting your local Department of Home Affairs office.

Get your new ID card photo with Smartphone iD

The Smartphone iD app allows you to take your ID photo from the comfort of your own home. Simply download the app, follow the guided instructions, and let our advanced AI system and team of biometric experts ensure your photo meets all the necessary requirements. Our service is affordable and delivers your photo instantly, so you can complete your ID card application with confidence and ease.

item.title: How to renew your driving license in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Is your South African driving license about to expire? In that case, it’s important to renew it before it expires, in order to avoid penalties and maintain your legal right to drive. In this article, we'll walk you through the process of renewing your driving license in South Africa, including when and where to renew, the documents you need, and how our app can help simplify the process.

When to renew your driving license

In South Africa, driving licenses are valid for five years from the date of issue. It's important to renew your license before it expires. You can renew your license up to four weeks before the expiration date. If your license has already expired, there is a 21-day grace period during which you can still renew it, but you may face additional penalties.

Where to apply for a new driving license

To renew your driving license, you need to visit a Driving License Testing Centre (DLTC) in person. There are DLTCs located throughout South Africa. You can find the nearest one to you by visiting the official website of the Road Traffic Management Corporation (RTMC) or by contacting your local municipality.

Can you renew your driving license online?

Unfortunately, it is not currently possible to renew your driving license online in South Africa. You must visit a DLTC in person to complete the renewal process. However, you can book an online appointment at some DLTCs to minimize your wait time.

How to renew your driving license

Follow the following steps to renew your driving license:

  1. Gather the required documents (see below) and locate your nearest DLTC.
  2. Visit the DLTC and complete the renewal application form. Book an appointment online if possible to save time.
  3. Take an eye test and pay the renewal fee at the designated counter.
  4. Have your photo and fingerprints taken for your new license card.
  5. Receive a temporary driving license on the spot. Your official card will be mailed to you within 4-6 weeks.

Documents needed to renew your driving license

When renewing your driving license, you will need to provide the following documents:

  • Your current driving license card
  • Your valid South African ID book, card, or passport
  • Proof of residential address, e.g. a utility bill
  • Two identical color passport photos (more on this below)

Cost to renew your driving license

As of 2024, the cost to renew a driving license card in South Africa is R140. There may be additional fees for booking, an eye test, and having photos taken, so be prepared to pay around R250-R300 in total. Payment can be made via cash, check or credit/debit card.

Driving license renewal processing time

The actual driving license renewal process at the DLTC takes about 2-3 hours, assuming there are no long queues. You'll be issued a temporary driving license on the spot which is valid for six weeks. Your new driving license card will be mailed to you within 4-6 weeks. If it doesn't arrive, check with the DLTC.

Get your new driving license quickly with Smartphone iD

One of the key requirements for your driving license renewal are two identical color passport photos. Getting proper passport photos can be a hassle, but our Smartphone iD app makes it quick and affordable. Simply download the app, take your photo, and get it digitally verified and delivered to your phone within minutes. At the moment, the Smartphone iD app is the most cost effective and passport photo solution in South Africa. Download the app and try it out for yourself!

item.title: A guide to the University of Johannesburg Application Form for 2025
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Applying to the University of Johannesburg (UJ) can be an exciting yet daunting process. To ensure a successful submission, it's of critical importance to fully understand the application form and requirements. This comprehensive guide will walk you through the UJ application process, providing you with all the necessary information and tips to make your application stand out.

What you need before applying

Before diving into the application process, there are a few important steps to take:

  1. Decide on your program: Research the various faculties and departments at UJ to find the program that aligns with your interests and career goals. UJ offers a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs across its four campuses.
  2. Check the entry requirements: Each program has specific entry requirements, such as minimum grades, subject prerequisites, and language proficiency. Make sure you meet these requirements before applying.
  3. Gather your documents: Prepare all the necessary documents, including your ID, academic transcripts, proof of address, and any additional documents required for your specific program.

When to apply

The application period for the 2025 academic year opens in April 2024. It's crucial to apply as early as possible, as some programs have limited spaces and operate on a first-come, first-served basis. Be sure to check the specific closing dates for your chosen program.

How to apply for UJ

UJ offers two application methods:

  1. Online Application: This is the preferred and free method. You can access the online application portal through the UJ website. The online system is user-friendly and allows you to track your application status.
  2. Paper Application: Downloadable application forms are available on the UJ website. However, a non-refundable application fee applies to paper submissions. We recommend using the online application method to save time and money.

The UJ online application form

The online application form consists of several sections:

  1. Personal information: Fill in your personal details, including your name, ID number, contact information, and address.
  2. Academic history: Provide details of your previous education, including your high school and any tertiary education.
  3. Program selection: Choose your preferred program and campus. You can select up to two program choices.
  4. Additional information: Answer questions related to your background, such as your home language, disability status, and funding requirements.
  5. Attachments: Upload the required documents, such as your ID, academic transcripts, and proof of address.

Required documents

To complete your application, you'll need to submit the following documents:

  1. A certified copy of your ID or passport
  2. Your academic transcripts
  3. Proof of address
  4. Any additional documents required for your specific program

Make sure to have these documents ready before starting your application.

Fees

The application fee for UJ varies depending on your program and application method. Online applications are free, while paper applications incur a non-refundable fee. Be sure to check the specific fees for your chosen program on the UJ website.

Get your UJ student card quickly with Smartphone iD

Once you've been accepted to UJ, you'll need a student card to access campus facilities and services. With Smartphone iD, you can get your student card photo taken quickly and easily. Our app ensures that your photo meets all the biometric requirements, and our team of experts verifies each photo before submission. Plus, our service is more affordable than traditional photo studios. Hence, if you want to save time and money on getting your passport photos, then the Smartphone iD app is your best option. 

Important tips

To ensure a smooth and successful application process, keep these important tips in mind:

  1. Meet deadlines: Make sure to submit your application before the closing date for your chosen program. Late applications may not be considered.
  2. Be truthful: Provide accurate and honest information in your application. Any discrepancies may lead to your application being rejected.
  3. Proofread: Double-check your application for any errors or missing information before submitting.
  4. Keep a copy: Save a copy of your application and all submitted documents for your records.

By carefully following the steps that are described in this guide, you'll be well on your way to a successful application to the University of Johannesburg. Good luck with your application!

item.title: How to renew your firearms license in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Renewing your license is an important part of maintaining your right to legally own and use firearms. In this article, we'll walk you through the key steps and requirements for renewing your firearms license, including when and where to apply, what documents you'll need, and how much it costs. We'll also share some helpful tips to make the renewal process as smooth as possible.


When to apply for firearms license renewal

It's important to apply for your firearms license renewal before your current license expires. According to the Firearms Control Act 60 of 2000, you must submit your renewal application at least 90 days before the expiration date of your existing license. We recommend starting the process even earlier to allow ample time to gather the necessary documents and complete the application. Your renewed license will be valid for a period of five years from the date of issue.

Where to apply for firearms license renewal

Firearms license renewal applications must be submitted in person at your nearest Designated Firearms Officer (DFO). DFOs are located at police stations across South Africa. When you go to submit your application, be sure to bring along all the required documents (detailed below). The DFO will review your application and supporting materials. If anything is missing or incomplete, they will let you know what else is needed to proceed with the renewal process.

How to apply for firearms license renewal

To apply for a firearms license renewal in South Africa, follow these steps:

  1. Obtain the SAPS 517(a) application form from your nearest Designated Firearms Officer (DFO) or download it from the official SAPS website.
  2. Fill out the application form completely and accurately in black ink.
  3. Gather the required supporting documents to submit with your application form.
  4. Double-check that your application form is complete and that you have all the necessary supporting documents.
  5. Submit your completed application form and supporting documents in person at your nearest DFO.
  6. Pay the applicable renewal fee by cash or bank-guaranteed cheque.
  7. Receive a receipt for your payment and keep it for your records.

Documents needed for firearms license renewal

When submitting your firearms license renewal application, you'll need to provide the following documents:

  • Your current firearms license
  • A certified copy of your ID document
  • Proof of residence (e.g. a utility bill or bank statement)
  • Proof of proficiency with the firearm type (e.g. a training certificate)
  • Two color passport photos

Cost of firearms license renewal

The fee for renewing a firearms license in South Africa is R70. This amount must be paid when submitting your renewal application at the DFO. Be sure to check the latest fees before applying, as they are subject to change. The renewal fee is payable by cash or bank-guaranteed cheque. Once your payment is processed, you'll receive a receipt which you should keep for your records.

Processing time for firearms license renewal

After submitting your firearms license renewal application and supporting documents, your information will be reviewed by the relevant authorities. The expected processing time is around 90 days, although it may take longer in some cases. If your application is approved, your new license card will be mailed to you. Be sure to keep an eye out for it and contact the police if you don't receive it within a reasonable timeframe after approval.

Get a new firearms license quickly with Smartphone iD

Smartphone iD makes it quick and convenient to obtain a passport photo for your firearms license application. With our app you can capture a compliant passport photo right from your smartphone. After you take your photo, it will be reviewed by our advanced AI system and team of experts to make sure that it meets all the necessary requirements. Download the app now and receive your firearms license photos within a couple of minutes!

Are you a South African citizen looking to apply for a new passport? Then we have good news. It's now possible to apply for your passport online from the comfort of your own home. In this article, we'll guide you through the process of applying for a South African passport online. Additionally, we'll show you the most convenient solution for capturing your passport photo.

Can I apply for a South African passport online?

Yes, South African citizens can apply for their passports online through the eHomeAffairs portal. This service allows you to complete the application process, make payments, and schedule an appointment for biometric capture at a participating bank branch. By applying online, you can save time and avoid the hassle of visiting a Home Affairs office.

How to apply for a passport online

To apply for your South African passport online, follow these steps:

  1. Visit the eHomeAffairs website and create an account: https://ehome.dha.gov.za/ehomeaffairsv3
  2. Log in to your account and select the "Passport Application" option.
  3. Complete the online application form with your personal details, contact information, and passport preferences.
  4. Upload the required documents (see next paragraph)
  5. Make the necessary payment for your passport application using a credit or debit card.
  6. Schedule an appointment at a participating bank branch for biometric capture.
  7. Attend your appointment, where your fingerprints and signature will be captured.
  8. Your passport will be processed and delivered to your chosen collection point.

Required documents for an online passport application

When applying for your South African passport online, you'll need to provide the following documents:

  • A copy of your South African ID document
  • Proof of residential address, such as a utility bill or bank statement
  • A recent passport photo that meets the Department of Home Affairs' requirements

item.title: Passport price in South Africa: Get the details
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Are you wondering about the cost of getting a passport in South Africa? The price depends on several factors, including age, number of pages, and where you're applying from. In this article, we'll break down the various passport prices in South Africa and explain how Smartphone iD can help you save money on your passport photos.

Adult passport (32 pages)

The cost of a 32-page adult passport in South Africa is R600 when applying inside the country. If you're applying from outside South Africa, the price is R1200. Keep in mind that this is just the cost of the passport itself - you'll also need to factor in the price of passport photos.

Adult passport (48 pages)

If you need more pages, you can opt for a 48-page adult passport instead. The price for this is R1200 when applying inside South Africa, or R2400 when applying from abroad. The 48-page option is a good choice for frequent travelers who need extra space for visa stamps.

Child passport

For children under 16, the price of a South African passport is R600 when applying domestically, or R1200 when applying from outside the country. Note that children's passports are only valid for 5 years, compared to 10 years for adult passports.

Official passport

Official passports are issued to government officials traveling abroad on state business. The price for an official passport is R600 when applying within South Africa. For applications made outside the country, the cost is R1200.

Diplomatic passport

Diplomatic passports are reserved for high-ranking government officials, diplomats, and their families. The cost of a diplomatic passport is also R600 when applying inside South Africa, or R1200 when applying from abroad.

Document for travel purposes

In some cases, you may be able to get a temporary travel document instead of a full passport. This document allows a single journey to or from South Africa. The price is R400 when applying domestically, or R800 when applying outside the country.

Crew member certificate

Crew member certificates are issued to air and sea crew traveling for work purposes. The price of a crew member certificate is R350 when applying within South Africa, or R700 when applying from abroad.

What is the price of passport photos in South Africa?

In addition to the passport fees, you'll also need to pay for passport photos. Most photo studios charge around R60-R150 for a set of passport photos. However, you can save money by taking your own passport photos with Smartphone iD.

Our app guides you to take passport photos with your smartphone that meet all the official requirements, and it's cheaper than going to a photo studio. Plus, our team of biometric experts and advanced AI system checks each photo to ensure it will be accepted. So if you want to get your South African passport at an affordable price, give Smartphone iD a try. We make it easy and inexpensive to take your own high-quality passport photos from home.

item.title: How long does it take to get a passport in South Africa?
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Are you planning an international trip and need to get your passport sorted out? Wondering how long the passport application process takes in South Africa? In this article, we've got you covered with all the details on passport processing times, whether you're applying for a new passport domestically or abroad, or submitting your application online.

Processing times for different types of passports in South Africa

The amount of time it takes to get your passport in South Africa depends on the type of passport you are applying for:

  • Tourist passports: Applications are typically processed within 10-15 working days.
  • Maxi tourist passports (48 pages): Processing usually takes 15-20 working days.
  • Official/diplomatic passports: Expect processing to be completed in 5-10 working days in most cases.
  • Emergency travel documents: These can often be issued the same day or within 1-2 working days when justified.

Keep in mind that during peak travel periods like the December holidays, processing times may be longer than usual due to high demand. Applying well in advance of your planned travel dates is advisable.

Passport processing times when applying abroad

South African citizens who are currently overseas can apply for a passport at their nearest South African embassy, consulate or mission. Processing times vary by location and type of passport, but are generally in the range of 10-20 working days once all required documents have been submitted. Check with your local South African consular services for specific timelines.

Some South African missions abroad offer the option of submitting passport applications online via the eHomeAffairs portal, which can help streamline the process. However, you'll still need to make an appointment to visit the mission in person to complete your application.

Online passport application processing times

The Department of Home Affairs offers an online passport application system for South African citizens called eHomeAffairs. Through this portal, you can complete most of the passport application process digitally, including submitting your application form, making payments, and uploading supporting documents.

After completing the online application, you will need to schedule an appointment at your nearest Home Affairs office to finalize the process, have your biometrics captured, and submit any physical documents. Online applications are usually processed within 10 working days from the time of your in-person appointment. 

When applying for your passport, the photo you submit is a crucial element. With Smartphone iD, you can quickly and easily take your passport photo from anywhere using just your phone!

item.title: How to get an emergency passport in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Are you in urgent need of a passport in South Africa? In this article, we'll guide you through the process of obtaining an emergency passport in South Africa, including the required documents, processing time, and cost. We'll also share the fastest and most cost-effective way of obtaining your emergency passport photos.

Can I get an emergency passport in South Africa?

Yes, it is possible to obtain an emergency passport in South Africa. The Department of Home Affairs issues emergency passports, also known as temporary passports, to South African citizens who have an urgent need to travel and cannot wait for a standard passport application to be processed. However, emergency passports are only valid for a limited period and have certain restrictions compared to regular passports.

How to get an emergency passport in South Africa

To apply for an emergency passport in South Africa, follow these steps:

  1. Gather the required documents (see below).
  2. Visit your nearest Department of Home Affairs office that offers passport services.
  3. Complete the application form (DHA-73) and submit it along with the required documents.
  4. Pay the applicable fee for an emergency passport.
  5. Wait for your emergency passport to be processed and issued.

The required documents for an emergency passport application in South Africa include:

  • A completed application form (DHA-73)
  • Your original South African ID document or a certified copy
  • Proof of urgency, such as a letter from your employer or a medical certificate
  • Two recent passport photographs that meet the Department of Home Affairs' requirements
  • The applicable fee for an emergency passport

How long does an emergency passport take in South Africa?

The processing time for an emergency passport in South Africa is typically faster than a standard passport application. In most cases, you can expect to receive your emergency passport within 1-2 working days after submitting your application and required documents. However, processing times may vary depending on the workload of the Department of Home Affairs office you visit and the complexity of your case.

How much is an emergency passport in South Africa?

The cost of an emergency passport in South Africa is higher than a standard passport. As of 2024, the fee for an emergency passport is R600. This fee is subject to change, so it's always best to check with the Department of Home Affairs for the most up-to-date information on passport fees.

Simply download the Smartphone iD app and take your photo using your smartphone. After that, our advanced AI system, along with our team of experts, will ensure that your photo meets the Department of Home Affairs' requirements.

Within minutes, you'll receive your digital passport photo via email, ready to be used in your emergency passport application. By choosing the Smartphone iD app, you can save time and money while ensuring that your passport photo is of the highest quality and compliant with government standards.

item.title: How to get a USA visa from South Africa
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Are you a South African citizen planning to travel to the United States? If so, you'll need to obtain a valid visa before your trip. The visa application process can seem daunting, but with the right information and preparation, you can successfully secure your USA visa. In this article, we'll guide you through everything you need to know about applying for a USA visa from South Africa.

Do South African citizens need a visa for the USA?

Yes, South African citizens are required to obtain a visa to enter the United States for tourism, business, study, or other purposes. The type of visa you need depends on the purpose and duration of your trip. The most common types of visas for South African travelers are:

  • B1/B2 visa: For short-term business or tourism trips lasting up to 6 months
  • F1 visa: For full-time students studying at a US university or college
  • J1 visa: For participants in cultural exchange programs like au pair, intern, or summer work travel

When to apply for a U.S. visa

It's important to start the visa application process well in advance of your planned travel date. We recommend applying at least 3-4 months before your trip to allow enough time for processing and any potential delays. Keep in mind that visa interview appointments can fill up quickly, especially during Do South African citizens need a visa for the USA?

Yes, South African citizens are required to obtain a visa to enter the United States for tourism, business, study, or other purposes. The type of visa you need depends on the purpose and duration of your trip. The most common types of visas for South African travelers are:

  • B1/B2 visa: For short-term business or tourism trips lasting up to 6 months
  • F1 visa: For full-time students studying at a US university or college
  • J1 visa: For participants in cultural exchange programs like au pair, intern, or summer work travel

How to apply for a US visa

To apply for a US visa from South Africa, follow these steps:

  1. Determine the appropriate visa category for your trip purpose
  2. Complete the online nonimmigrant visa application form DS-160
  3. Pay the visa application fee (currently $160 USD)
  4. Schedule your visa interview appointment at the US Embassy or Consulate
  5. Gather the required documents for your visa interview
  6. Attend your visa interview and provide biometrics (fingerprints and photo)
  7. Wait for your visa to be processed and your passport to be returned

Documents required for a US visa application

When you attend your visa interview, you'll need to bring the following documents:

  • Valid passport with at least 6 months validity beyond your intended stay
  • Printed copy of your DS-160 confirmation page with barcode
  • Visa application fee payment receipt
  • One recent color passport-style photograph meeting US visa photo requirements
  • Supporting documents related to your purpose of travel (e.g. travel itinerary, proof of funds, employment letter, university acceptance letter, etc.)

US visa processing time

After your visa interview, the consular officer will inform you if your application requires additional administrative processing. Most visas are processed within 2-3 weeks, but some can take up to 6 weeks or longer depending on individual circumstances. You can check your visa application status online using the case number provided at your interview.

Tips to get your US visa approved

To increase your chances of getting your US visa application approved, keep these tips in mind:

  1. Be honest and consistent in your application and interview
  2. Provide strong ties to your home country to show you intend to return
  3. Demonstrate sufficient financial resources to cover your trip expenses
  4. Apply early to avoid delays or issues with travel plans
  5. Ensure your passport photo meets the strict US visa specifications

item.title: How to apply for an ID card online in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Are you looking to apply for a new Smart ID card in South Africa? While you can start the process online, you'll need to complete part of the application in person. In this guide, we'll walk you through how to apply for an ID card online and what steps you need to take to finalize your application at a Department of Home Affairs (DHA) office.

How to initiate your online ID card application

To begin your Smart ID card application online, you'll need to access the Department of Home Affairs' e-Services portal. Follow these steps to get started:

  1. Visit the official DHA e-Home Affairs portal.
  2. Create an account or log in if you already have one.
  3. Select "Smart ID Card" from the list of available services.
  4. Fill out the online application form with your personal details.
  5. Schedule an appointment at your nearest participating DHA office.
  6. Note down your reference number to track your application status.

Completing your ID card application in person

While the online portal allows you to begin the process and book an appointment, you'll need to visit a DHA office to submit your final application. Here's what to do:

  • Go to the DHA office on your scheduled appointment date.
  • Bring any original documents requested during the online application.
  • Pay the required application fee (check current fees on the DHA site).
  • Have your photograph and fingerprints captured for your new Smart ID card.

It's important to note that not all DHA offices currently support online appointment booking. Before starting your online application, we recommend checking the official DHA website for an updated list of offices offering this service.

Required documents for your ID card application

When you visit the DHA office to complete your Smart ID card application, you'll need to provide a few key documents:

  • Your existing green barcoded ID book (if you have one)
  • Your birth certificate
  • Proof of your residential address
  • If applicable, legal documents related to name changes

Get the perfect photo for your new ID card

When applying for your new Smart ID, submitting a high-quality photograph is essential. With Smartphone iD, you can easily take a biometric-standard ID photo right from your phone. Our app guides you to capture a picture that meets all official requirements. Plus, our team of experts will verify your photo to ensure it's ready for your ID application. Using the Smartphone iD app is quick, convenient, and the most affordable option on the market for ID pictures. Download the app today and check one important item off your ID application checklist!

item.title: How to replace a lost ID card in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Losing your ID card can be a stressful experience. In this article, we'll guide you through the steps to get a new ID card as quickly and easily as possible. We'll cover what to do if your ID card is lost, how to submit an application for a replacement, and where to go to complete the process. Let's get started on helping you replace your lost ID card.

What to do if your ID card is lost

If you've lost your South African ID card, follow these steps to report it and begin the replacement process:

  1. Report your ID card as lost or stolen at your nearest police station
  2. Provide basic information and sign an affidavit confirming your ID card is lost
  3. Obtain a case number from the police, which you'll need for your replacement ID card application
  4. Gather the required documents for your new ID card application
  5. Ensure your passport photo meets the Department of Home Affairs' strict requirements

Can you submit a lost ID card application online?

Unfortunately, you cannot submit an application for a lost ID card entirely online in South Africa. You'll need to visit a Department of Home Affairs office in person to complete the process. However, you can book an appointment online which can save you time and hassle. Just go to the Department of Home Affairs website and follow the prompts to schedule an appointment at your nearest branch.

Where to submit an application for a lost ID card

To apply for a replacement ID card, you'll need to go to a Department of Home Affairs branch. There are branches located throughout South Africa, so there should be one near you. Be sure to bring all the required documents, including your birth certificate, proof of address, and new passport photo. You'll also need to pay the application fee, which is currently R140.

How to replace a lost ID card

To replace your lost ID card in South Africa, follow these steps:

  1. Obtain the required documents and a compliant passport photo
  2. Book an appointment online at your nearest Department of Home Affairs branch to save time
  3. Complete the application form with accurate information
  4. Submit your completed application form, supporting documents, and passport photo to the Home Affairs official
  5. Have your biometrics captured by the Home Affairs official
  6. Pay the application fee
  7. Wait for your new ID card to be created and delivered, which may take a few weeks
  8. Request a temporary ID certificate from Home Affairs if you need proof of identity in the meantime

Sources

item.title: How to take the perfect baby passport photo in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Getting a passport for your baby is an important step in preparing for family travel. One critical aspect of the application process is providing a suitable baby passport photo that meets the strict requirements set by the South African Department of Home Affairs. In this article, we'll guide you through the process of capturing the perfect baby passport photo and ensuring a smooth application process.

Baby passport photo requirements and size in South Africa 

To ensure your baby's passport photo is accepted, it must meet the following requirements:

  • The photo should be in color and taken against a plain white or off-white background.
  • Your baby's face must be clearly visible and centered in the frame, with a neutral expression and both eyes open.
  • No objects, shadows, or other people should be visible in the photo.
  • The photo should measure 35mm x 45mm.
  • The baby's head should be between 25mm and 35mm from the chin to the crown.
  • The photo should be printed on high-quality photo paper with no creases, scratches, or other damage.

Where to take a biometric baby passport photo in South Africa

While you can take your baby's passport photo at home, it's recommended to use a professional service to ensure the photo meets all the necessary requirements. Smartphone iD is the best option for taking biometric baby passport photos in South Africa. We use advanced AI technology to ensure your photo is compliant with government standards, and our user-friendly app makes the process quick and easy. Simply take the photo using your smartphone, and our app will guide you through the process step-by-step.

The cost of a baby passport photo 

Taking your baby's passport photo with Smartphone iD is not only convenient but also cost-effective. Traditional photo studios often charge between R150 to R200 for a single passport photo, while photo booths can cost around R100 to R150. In comparison, we offer the most competitive prices on the market, while ensuring that you get a high-quality, compliant photo without breaking the bank. Plus, with our app, you can take as many photos as needed to get the perfect shot, without any additional fees

Common mistakes that lead to baby passport photo rejection 

To avoid having your baby's passport photo rejected, be sure to avoid these common mistakes:

  1. The baby's eyes are closed or not clearly visible.
  2. The baby's face is not centered in the frame or is too small/large.
  3. There are shadows or reflections on the baby's face.
  4. The background is not plain white or off-white.
  5. The photo is not printed on high-quality photo paper or has visible damage.

How to check your baby passport photo before submitting the application 

Before submitting your baby's passport application, it's crucial to ensure the photo meets all the necessary requirements. With Smartphone iD's passport photo checker, you can easily verify that your photo is compliant. Our advanced AI system analyzes the photo and provides instant feedback on any potential issues, allowing you to make adjustments before submitting the application. Additionally, our team of biometric experts reviews each photo to ensure it meets the guidelines set by the South African Department of Home Affairs.

With the advent of smartphone passport photo apps, you can now take your own passport photos from the comfort of your home. In this article, we'll guide you through the process of choosing the right app, taking the perfect photo, and ensuring that your passport application is accepted without any issues.

Choosing the right passport photo app

When selecting a passport photo app, consider the following features:

  • Size adjustment: The app should automatically resize your photo to meet the specific requirements of your country and document type.
  • Background change: Look for an app that can replace the background of your photo with a plain white or off-white background.
  • Basic editing tools: Basic tools like brightness, contrast, and cropping can help you achieve the perfect photo.

Advanced features to look for include AI-powered editing, multi-photo printing, and digital downloads. Consider the user interface and reviews, prioritizing ease of use and positive user feedback. Lastly, consider the cost – while some apps offer free options, paid apps may provide more features and higher-quality results.

What is the correct size of a digital passport photo?

When submitting a digital passport photo electronically, it's crucial to ensure that the image meets the required specifications. The digital photo should have a resolution of 600 DPI (dots per inch) to guarantee clarity and sharpness. This high resolution allows for accurate reproduction of your facial features, which is essential for identification purposes.

How to take a digital passport photo yourself

If you prefer to take your digital passport photo at home, follow these simple steps:

  1. Find a plain white or off-white background with adequate lighting.

  4. Remove any accessories such as hats, sunglasses, or large jewelry.
  5. Use a digital camera or smartphone with at least 5 megapixels for the best results.

Alternatively, you can use an online service like the Smartphone iD app to effortlessly take your digital passport photo. Our app guides you through the process step-by-step, ensuring that your photo meets all the necessary requirements.

item.title: How to take a passport photo for your South African permanent residence permit
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Are you applying for a South African Permanent Residence Permit? One of the key requirements is providing a suitable passport photo. But what exactly are the photo specifications, and what's the easiest way to get a photo that meets all the official requirements? In this guide, we'll walk you through everything you need to know to take the perfect passport photo for your Permanent Residence Permit application.

Photo size and specifications

The passport photo for your South African Permanent Residence Permit must meet the following size requirements:

  • You must have a neutral facial expression with your mouth closed and eyes open and clearly visible
  • High-quality photo paper is essential for printing your passport photo
  • Your face should occupy about 70-80% of the total photo area
  • Ensure your facial features are clearly visible
  • Pay attention to lighting to avoid shadows or glare on your face
  • The photo must measure 35mm wide by 45mm tall
  • Your head should take up between 29mm to 34mm of the photo vertically, from the top of your hair to your chin
  • The photo must be in color, clear and in sharp focus, with no blurriness, pixelation, or graininess
  • The photo must be taken against a plain white or off-white background with no shadows

Number of photos required

When applying for your South African Permanent Residence Permit, you need to submit two identical copies of your passport photo. Both photos must be recent (taken within the last 6 months) and meet all the official size and quality specifications. We recommend getting a couple extra copies of your photo in case you make a mistake when attaching them to your application.

Submitting your photo with your application

When you have your passport photos ready, you'll need to attach them to your Permanent Residence Permit application in the designated spots. Use paperclips rather than staples to avoid damaging the photos or application. Make sure the photos are firmly attached and will not fall off during processing.

item.title: Renouvellement du permis de conduire sur l’ANTS
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
Le renouvellement d’un permis de conduire en France peut se faire en ligne depuis 2019 via le site de l’Agence Nationale des titres Sécurisés (ATNS). 

La date d'expiration de votre titre du permis de conduire se trouve en ligne 4b. Il est donc nécessaire de renouveler votre titre et d'entamer les démarches avant cette date! 

Comment renouveler son permis de conduire sur l’ANTS (permis A et B) ? 

Afin d’effectuer une demande de renouvellement de permis de conduire en ligne : 

  1. Il convient de vous rendre en ligne sur le site de l’agence nationale des titres sécurisés (ANTS) : https://permisdeconduire.ants.gouv.fr/. 
  2. Il existe ensuite deux façon d’accéder à votre espace personnel : 
  • vous possédez un compte ANTS (ou vous en créez un), 
  • ou vous pouvez vous connecter avec FranceConnect.
  1. Une fois que vous êtes connecté, rendez vous dans la rubrique “Commencer une nouvelle démarche en ligne” et dans l’onglet “Permis de conduire”. 
  2. Ensuite, sélectionnez le motif de votre demande. Pour le renouvellement de votre permis de conduire, vous devez sélectionner l’option pour la fabrication d’un titre de permis de conduire. 
  1. Choisissez ensuite la personne concernée et le motif “renouvellement de titre”.
  1. Quel est le motif de votre renouvellement ? Perte ou vol de votre permis, remplacement d’un permis détérioré ou d’un permis pliant 3 volets, changement d’état civil ou fin de validité du permis. 
  1. Joignez-y votre certificat médical si nécessaire : 
  • en cas de permis C1, C1E, C, CE, D1, D1E, D ou DE,
  • si vous êtes titulaire d'une pension d'invalidité civile ou militaire, 
  • si vous demandez une catégorie lourde (C1, C1E, C, CE, D1, D1E, D ou DE), 
  • si vous êtes atteint d'une affection et/ou d'un handicap susceptible d'être incompatible avec l'obtention ou le maintien du permis de conduire
  1. Accédez ensuite à la deuxième étape consacrée à la saisine de l'état civil. 
  1. Une troisième étape est alors consacrée à l’adresse et les coordonnées de la personne concernée par la demande de renouvellement de passeport.
  2. Transmission de la photo d’identité et signature numérique. Grâce à SMARTPHONE ID, transmettez directement votre photo numérique. Nos services vous permettront de ne pas avoir à envoyer votre photo au format papier à l’administration pour le renouvellement de votre permis de conduire. 
  3. Transmission de vos pièces justificatives 
  4. Récapitulatif de votre demande et confirmation 

Quelles pièces justificatives pour renouveler son permis de conduire ? 

Afin d’opérer le renouvellement de votre permis de conduire, il est nécessaire de transmettre les pièces justificatives suivantes (quelque soit le motif de renouvellement) : 

  • Une copie de votre pièce d'identité en cours de validité 
  • Un justificatif de domicile de moins 6 mois 
  • Une photo-signature numérique 
  • Un formulaire d’avis médical si nécessaire (demande de permis catégorie du groupe lourd, suite à une intervention chirurgicale ou encore si le titre de conduite est soumis à avis médical) : https://www.service-public.fr/simulateur/calcul/14880 

Renouvellement des permis poids lourds et transports en commun sur ANTS 

Afin de renouveler la validité de son permis poids-lourd (C1, C1E, C, CE, D1, D1E, D ou DE), vous devez effectuer une visite médicale. 

Le médecin doit être agréé par la préfecture de votre lieu de résidence. Il ne doit pas être votre médecin traitant. 

Vous pouvez consulter la liste des médecins agréés sur le site internet ici.

Vous pourrez ensuite vous rendre en ligne sur le site de l’agence nationale des titres sécurisés (ANTS) : https://permisdeconduire.ants.gouv.fr/. Connectez-vous, choisissez le motif “renouvellement du permis de conduire”. 

Choisissez la catégorie de votre permis (C, D ou EC). Remplissez le formulaire de demande de renouvellement en indiquant vos informations personnelles, votre adresse et vos coordonnées.

Joindre les pièces justificatives demandées.

Valider votre demande et payer la redevance de fabrication du permis.

Vous recevrez un e-mail de confirmation de votre demande.

Renouvellement de mon permis suite à sa suspension 

Afin d’effectuer une demande de renouvellement de permis de conduire suite à sa suspension, il convient de se rendre en ligne sur le site de l’agence nationale des titres sécurisés (ANTS) : https://permisdeconduire.ants.gouv.fr/. La demande de renouvellement doit être effectuée à la fin de la période de suspension. 

Une fois connecté, cliquez successivement sur : nouvelle demande, le permis de conduire, je commence la demande. 

Veuillez ensuite choisir le motif de votre demande : "Je demande la fabrication d'un titre de permis de conduire", puis complétez les informations de la personne concernée dont le permis a été suspendu. 

Fournissez ensuite vos pièces justificatives. Le demandeur doit alors transmettre : 

  • une pièce d’identité, 
  • une photo-signature numérique, 
  • la décision préfectorale de suspension du permis de conduire,
  • un justificatif de domicile de moins de 6 mois (attestation d’hébergement avec CNI de l’hébergeant, facture d’énergie ou téléphonique), 
  • un avis médical si nécessaire (par exemple, en cas d’infraction de conduite liée à l'alcool ou aux stupéfiants)

Lisez ensuite le récapitulatif de votre demande et validez votre démarche. 

Obtenez votre nouveau permis rapidement avec Smartphone ID 

Avec notre application Smartphone iD, il vous est possible d’effectuer votre renouvellement rapidement grâce au code e-photo  ANTS. Ainsi, votre photo d’identité numérique sera prête en quelques minutes depuis votre smartphone, et donc sans sortir de chez vous !

Nos services respectent les normes de l’OACI et de l’ANTS pour vos e-photos permis de conduire. 

Vous recevrez un code numérique unique par e-mail quelques minutes après la validation de votre photo d'identité prise par notre application avec nos experts biométriques et notre système avancé d’IA. Nos services vous permettront d’accélérer votre demande de renouvellement sur le site de l'ANTS. Tout cela à prix abordable et depuis chez vous ! 

FAQS

Quelle est la durée de validité de mon nouveau permis de conduire ?

Le renouvellement du permis de conduite avec catégorie A ou B est valable 15 ans.

Le renouvellement du permis poids lourds et du permis transport de personnes est valable 5 ans.

Est-il possible de réaliser la demande de renouvellement par courrier ?

Si vous vivez en France, non. 

La visite médicale est-elle obligatoire pour le renouvellement en ligne ?

Non, sauf en cas de demande de permis groupe lourd (C1, C1E, C, CE, D1, D1E, D ou DE), suite à une intervention chirurgicale, ou encore si le titre de conduite est soumis à avis médical (par exemple, en cas d’infraction au code de la conduite). 

Mon permis a expiré. Comment le renouveler ?

Préparez en amont votre photo d’identité signature numérique avec Smartphone ID, puis rendez vous sur le site de l’ANTS : https://permisdeconduire.ants.gouv.fr/

Demandez en ligne un nouveau permis de conduire en cas de fin de validité : démarche en ligne accessible avec FranceConnect ou avec vos identifiants ANTS. 

Le renouvellement des permis B et A nécessite-t-il un examen médical?

Non.

item.title: Renouvellement de la carte d’identité: Guide complet
item.dc:creator: Karen
item.content:encoded:
La date d'expiration de votre carte d'identité se trouve sur votre carte (exception pour les cartes prorogées). Il est donc nécessaire de renouveler votre titre et d'entamer les démarches avant cette date. Vous trouverez ici toutes les informations concernant les étapes à suivre pour le renouvellement de votre carte d’identité française. 

Pré-demande pour un renouvellement de carte d'identité

Si vous êtes en France et que vous souhaitez renouveler votre carte d’identité, vous pouvez effectuer une pré-demande en ligne (accessible avec un compte ANTS ou via France Connect). Cette démarche n’est pas obligatoire mais facilite votre demande. Rendez-vous ici : https://passeport.ants.gouv.fr/demarches-en-ligne/effectuer-le-renouvellement-de-votre-carte-didentite. 

Comment renouveler sa carte d'identité ?

Renouveler sa carte d’identité en France 

Vous devrez vous présenter en mairie pour finaliser votre demande, en personne. Toutes les mairies habilitées ici : https://passeport.ants.gouv.fr/services/geolocaliser-une-mairie-habilitee 

Ensuite, la mairie se charge de prendre vos empreintes et de vérifier vos pièces justificatives. Durant le rendez-vous, votre présence est indispensable. 

La carte d'identité n'est pas fabriquée sur place : il faudra donc la retirer personnellement une fois qu’elle est prête. 

Pour suivre l’avancement de votre demande : https://www.service-public.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/R49786 

Renouveler sa carte d’identité à l’étranger 

Si vous êtes à l’étranger et que vous souhaitez renouveler votre carte d’identité, vous devez vous rendre dans les consulats équipés d’une station d’enregistrement. 

Rapprochez-vous de votre consulat pour les modalités de rendez-vous et le dépôt de votre dossier. En effet, le service peut exiger que le dépôt du dossier se fasse uniquement sur rendez-vous ! Votre présence est indispensable pour procéder à la prise d'empreintes durant le rendez-vous.

Vous devez ensuite retirer personnellement votre nouvelle carte d'identité une fois qu’elle est prête. Pour suivre l’avancement de votre demande : https://www.service-public.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/R49786 

Quelles pièces justificatives pour renouveler sa carte d'identité ? 

Pour le renouvellement d’une carte d’identité d’une personne majeure, vous devez présenter les documents suivants (selon les cas) : 

Notez qu'il est obligatoire de se présenter personnellement pour déposer une demande de renouvellement de carte d’identité.

Pour plus d'informations concernant les pièces justificatives, veuillez consulter le guide en ligne proposé par service-public.fr.

Quel prix pour renouveler ma carte d'identité ? 

La demande de renouvellement de carte nationale d'identité est gratuite.

En cas de perte de votre carte nationale d'identité, vous devrez payer un timbre fiscal de 25 euros, en vue de son renouvellement. Prévoyez également le paiement de votre photo d’identité. 

Quel délai pour renouveler ma carte d'identité ? 

Les délais de fabrication de la carte d’identité peuvent prendre plusieurs semaines. Les demandes sont accrues en période d’été. 

À l’étranger, le délai est de deux à quatre semaines. 

Afin de suivre l’avancement de votre demande, rendez-vous ici : https://www.service-public.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/R49786 

Comment retirer ma carte d'identité ? 

Vous devez retirer en personne votre nouvelle carte d’identité dans la mairie de dépôt de votre dossier. Vous devez rendre votre ancienne carte. 

Votre carte doit être retirée dans les 3 mois. Passé ce délai, elle sera détruite.

Votre nouvelle carte d’identité est valide 10 ans. 

Comment obtenir rapidement ma carte d'identité ? 

En utilisant notre application Smartphone ID ! Son utilisation permet l'obtention d’une photo conforme aux normes de l’ANTS pour votre carte d’identité. 

Votre photo de moins de 6 mois en format numérique sera envoyée à votre boîte email.

Vous pouvez ajouter une demande dans l'application Smartphone ID  pour que votre planche photo d'identité numérique soit imprimée sur papier de haute qualité, et livrée à votre adresse rapidement (de 2 à 5 jours en France). 

Les photos sont contrôlées par des experts, et systèmes d’intelligence artificielle avant de vous être envoyées. 

Tout cela pour un prix abordable ! Notre solution vous évite ainsi de vous déplacer chez un photographe professionnel, et vous permet de gagner du temps précieux dans le processus de renouvellement de votre CNI ! 

FAQ

Quand faire la demande de renouvellement ?

Vous pouvez demander le renouvellement de votre carte d’identité dès l'année qui précède la date d'expiration de votre carte d'identité actuelle.

La demande de renouvellement de la carte d'identité est-elle gratuite ?

Oui, à condition de pouvoir présenter votre ancienne carte. 

Comment faire le renouvellement de la carte d'identité d'un mineur ?

Faites une pré-demande en ligne, prenez rendez-vous dans une mairie habilitée et préparez toutes vos pièces justificatives. 

Quelle est la période de validité de la carte d'identité d'un mineur?

10 ans
